This is maloya. 18th century to present.
on_screen: Title card: maloya · France · 18th century to present

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Maloya originated in the 18th century among enslaved people from Madagascar and East Africa.
It was practiced in secret to resist oppression and honor ancestors.
It was banned by the French administration until the 1980s due to its association with the Communist Party and autonomist movements.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Used for ancestral worship (servis kabaré) and as a vehicle for political and social protest against slavery and poverty.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Traditional instrumentation includes the roulèr, kayamb, pikér, sati, and bob.
Modern versions may include djembes, synthesizers, and guitars.
Listen for the roulèr, kayamb, pikér, sati.
The pulse is Ternary.

A percussive, acoustic sound dominated by the deep resonance of the roulèr drum, the rattling of the kayamb, and the rhythmic striking of bamboo and metal idiophones, often featuring a lead vocalist answered by a chorus.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of maloya (France). Meter Ternary. Instruments: roulèr, kayamb, pikér, sati, bob. Vocal style: Call-response between soloist and choir. Form: Song of lament or protest. Mood: protest, ancestral, festive, melancholic. It should sound like this: A percussive, acoustic sound dominated by the deep resonance of the roulèr drum, the rattling of the kayamb, and the rhythmic striking of bamboo and metal idiophones, often featuring a lead vocalist answered by a chorus. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.
